answer: There are a few things I am proud of, but one stands out above the rest. An achievement I am genuinely proud of was completing a challenging professional qualification while working full time. It was a certificate course in international student counselling, which I finished last year to become better at my job. Balancing study with a demanding job was far harder than I had anticipated. For nearly a year, I sacrificed most of my evenings and weekends, which required real [[discipline]]. I would come home from the office, have dinner with my family and then [[burn the midnight oil]] at my desk, often with a cup of tea going cold beside me. There were moments when I felt like giving up, especially when the material seemed impossibly difficult. On those nights, a quick walk by the river usually helped me clear my head and start again. What kept me going was a stubborn [[determination]] to finish what I had started. When I finally passed the final exam, the sense of relief and pride was overwhelming. My father was so delighted that he bought sweets for half the neighbourhood. What made it so meaningful was that I had earned it entirely through my own effort and [[persistence]]. Honestly, that accomplishment gave me a huge confidence boost and proved to myself that I could handle serious challenges. It remains one of my proudest moments, not because of the qualification itself, but because of the [[resilience]] it took to get there. It taught me I am capable of far more than I thought.

followUps.q: Has the qualification helped you in your job?
followUps.answer: Yes, quite a lot. I feel more confident advising students now, especially about choosing courses and preparing for interviews, and my manager has started giving me some of the more complicated cases.

followUps.q: How did your family support you during that time?
followUps.answer: They were very patient. My mother kept bringing me tea late at night, and my younger sister, who is a serious student herself, often studied beside me, which kept both of us motivated.
